codex.relay_note: Evaluated via author's local authentication/metering gateway (127.0.0.1:3425/v1). External users can bind any OpenAI Responses-compatible model endpoint (e.g., gpt-5 / o3).

dsh.relay_note: Evaluated via internal DSH model endpoint. External users can bind any DeepSeek / OpenAI-compatible model endpoint.

statistical_caveats: All 18 engineering tasks (20 task.toml definitions including 3 Seed->Eval pairs) and their verifiers were constructed by the project authors from real vllm-ascend bugs and optimization bottlenecks.

Most (task, model, ablation_group) cells were evaluated with repetitions=1 due to live NPU and frontier reasoning token budgets; results represent controlled mechanism ablation evidence rather than a multi-repetition third-party blind benchmark.

In G3 (experience flywheel), 0/3 -> 1/1 on L2 cpu-rope-32 and L3 live NPU rope-32 refers to Codex CLI failing across G0, G1, and G2 (1 attempt each = 0/3) and passing on G3 (1/1) after retrieving the C6-distilled SOP from sibling seed task rope-64; on DSH, G0/G1/G2 also passed and G3 reduced delivery latency.

In G4 (open-ended exploration), 0/8 -> 8/8 covers 2 problem families (DeepSeek-V4 SparseMLA QLI fusion & Triton SpatialNorm 4D reduction) x 2 tiers (L2 local & L3 live NPU) x 2 models under knowledge_gradient='near_exact' factor-graph guidance and leave-one-out ablation gates.

In G2 (progressive disclosure), several tasks where the prompt/traceback already localized the fault showed higher wall-clock latency than G1 or G0 because extra knowledge_query/knowledge_explain calls added context and reasoning turns.
